codexReference.tileSet: The standard tile set has 144 tiles. Your chosen Wall and run effects can change its composition:
codexReference.windOrder: The Winds are listed in East, South, West, North order. All four use the same base point values.
codexReference.windPoints: Winds are Honor tiles worth {{points}} points each, or {{groupPoints}} per tile inside a group.
codexReference.honorGroups: Honors cannot form numbered sequences. Identical Honors can form pairs, triplets or quads.
codexReference.dragonPoints: Dragons are Honor tiles worth {{points}} points each. Every scoring Dragon adds +{{mult}} Mult, or +{{groupMult}} Mult inside a group. They cannot form numbered sequences.
codexReference.seasonDuration: Active only for the current round
codexReference.quadBonus: Adds +{{points}} group points and +{{mult}} pattern Mult, before tile effects.
codexReference.quadRefill: Play a quad as part of your selected hand. The rack refills after the play; there is no separate quad declaration action.
codexReference.winningExample: The four melds can be sequences, triplets or quads. Each quad adds one tile to the usual 14-tile structure. Here is an example without quads:
codexReference.sevenPairs: Exactly 7 different pairs: 14 tiles, with no triplets or sequences needed.
codexReference.thirteenOrphans: One of each terminal and Honor (13 unique tiles), plus one duplicate: a 14-tile Yakuman hand.
codexReference.wallSize: The wall supplies replacement tiles. Its remaining size depends on your Wall, starting rack and effects; watch the remaining tiles counter.
codexReference.yakuTiers: The current catalog has {{count}} Yaku in four tiers. These are their base multipliers, before upgrades and effects:
codexReference.allSimples: Contains only numbered tiles 2–8, with no terminals or Honors.
codexReference.allTriplets: All four melds are triplets or quads, with one pair and no sequences.
codexReference.fullFlush: Contains only one numbered suit, with no Honors.
codexReference.structuralHelp: Alter what makes a legal hand
codexReference.name: Name
codexReference.raritySources: Rarity affects shop availability and price. Heavenly Ordinances come from special sources, not ordinary shop offers. Build synergies and check each offer's actual price.
codexReference.decreeScrolls: Each Decree is an illustrated scroll. Tap one you own to read its effect while you plan.
codexReference.slotBaseline: The default is 5 Decree slots, but your chosen table and run effects can change that. Extra slots can come from:
codexReference.hierarchyOverride: When rules conflict, higher-authority rules take precedence over lower-authority rules. Check each effect's specific conditions.
codexReference.tipScore: Compare the score preview for groups of up to {{max}} tiles, or a complete Mahjong hand. Spend Turns on progress toward the target instead of waiting only for a perfect hand.
codexReference.tipSynergy: Decrees that work together can be stronger than powerful standalone Decrees.
codexReference.tipPurpose: Before buying, ask what you would keep or play differently if you owned it. An upgrade you can use beats a stronger one you can't trigger.
codexReference.tipEconomy: Saving Gold earns interest on a clear, but spend when an upgrade helps you reach the next target. Check actual prices and Sell values.
codexReference.tipFlowers: Flowers persist for the run. Two distinct Flowers grant a Decree slot; collecting all four strengthens their effects.
codexReference.tipYaku: Choose Yaku that fit your rack and Decrees. A complete Mahjong hand can combine Yaku for larger scores.
codexReference.tipEfficiency: Keep tiles that can complete several groups. Use REDRAW to replace isolated tiles, allowing for its Turn cost and any free redraws.
codexReference.tipWall: Check the river and remaining wall before chasing a specific tile. Redrawn tiles stay in the river for the rest of the round.
codexReference.tipMandate: Read the upcoming Boss Mandate and prepare a build that can score under its restriction.
codexReference.tipLoss: After a run, find one decision you would change, like a REDRAW spent too early or a tile kept without a plan, and try it next time.
codexReference.biggerHandP1: Every group after the first adds Mult, and a complete Mahjong hand adds the most. Instead of playing each small group as soon as it appears, keep the groups you have and REDRAW the spare tiles.
codexReference.biggerHandRack: This rack holds two finished sequences, two unfinished {{circles}} sequences and an {{east}} pair, plus two unmatched Dragons. One REDRAW sends both Dragons to the river.
codexReference.biggerHandComplete: If the new tiles are 1 and 4 of {{circles}}, the fourteen tiles make four sequences and a pair. Select all fourteen and play them: a finished hand does not score by itself.
codexReference.biggerHandWarning: Draws are random, and chasing a big hand can cost the round. Compare the score you can make now with the Turns you have left.
codexReference.congratulations: Congratulations! You now understand the fundamentals of Tensho.
codexReference.farewell: May the tiles favor you on your heavenly ascent!

codexEconomy.payout: Base clear rewards are 3 Gold for Small, 5 for Large and 10 for Boss rounds, not based on excess score. Stakes can remove the Small reward; Decrees and Omens can change the final payout.
codexEconomy.interest: Interest uses Gold held before the clear payout: 1 per 5, capped at 5 by default. Charters and Omens can raise the cap; some Omens block interest. Defeat pays no interest.
codexEconomy.sale: Inspect a Decree’s Sell button for its actual value. Flower-paid and free reward Decrees can sell for 0 Gold; Eternal Decrees cannot be sold. Selling removes its effects and frees the slot it used.
codexEconomy.prices: Use each offer’s displayed price and the current Reroll cost. Discounts, editions, Charters and other effects can change prices. Rerolls do not refresh purchased Charters or the free Cartomancer offer.

runJourney.optional: Victory is earned at the Act {{total}} Boss. Endless and higher Stakes are optional challenges, not requirements to finish the game.
runJourney.recommendation: For your first win, choose Green Felt and White Stake. Tables change rules, not just appearance; Stakes add difficulty. Red keeps White's targets but removes Small-round reward Gold.
runJourney.guideEarly: Start with reliable +Points and +Mult. Choose bonuses that trigger on the tiles and patterns you actually play, not a rare hand you hope to find.
runJourney.guideLate: Before the final Acts, look for Mult that grows across plays or rounds, then a ×Mult Decree to amplify it. More flat Points alone may not keep up.
runJourney.guideExample: Example: 100 Points × (4 Mult + 6 Mult) × 2 = 2,000 points. +Mult adds to the multiplier; ×Mult multiplies it. Combine both.
runJourney.guideMatch: Match conditions: a triplet bonus needs triplets; a suit bonus needs that suit. Read each scroll's rules. A powerful effect that never triggers is a wasted slot. Keep Gold for useful purchases instead of spending it all on rerolls.

decree-treasure-hunter.description: When you win a round, +1 Gold for each different suit left on your rack. Winds and Dragons count as separate suits.

decree-tax-collector.name: Tax Collector
decree-tax-collector.description: +4 Gold at the end of each round

decree-slow-burn.name: Slow Burn
decree-slow-burn.description: +2 Mult per round completed this run

decree-momentum.name: Momentum
decree-momentum.description: +15 Points for each earlier play this round

decree-crescendo.name: Crescendo
decree-crescendo.description: ×1.1 Mult for each earlier play this round

decree-waste-not.name: Waste Not
decree-waste-not.description: +5 Mult if you have not used REDRAW this round

decree-recycler.name: Recycler
decree-recycler.description: +10 Points per tile redrawn this round

decree-yakuhai-zealot.name: Value Zealot
decree-yakuhai-zealot.description: ×1.5 Mult when you score Value Tiles: a complete hand with a triplet or quad of Dragons or East Wind

decree-toitoi-titan.name: Triplet Titan
decree-toitoi-titan.description: ×1.5 Mult when you score All Triplets: a complete hand of four triplets or quads plus a pair

decree-ittsu-initiate.name: Ninefold Initiate
decree-ittsu-initiate.description: ×1.5 Mult when you score a 1–9 Straight: a complete hand holding 1-2-3, 4-5-6 and 7-8-9 of one suit

decree-chinitsu-champion.name: Full Flush Champion
decree-chinitsu-champion.description: ×2 Mult when you score a Full Flush: a complete hand of one suit only, with no Winds or Dragons

decree-wind-dragon.name: Wind and Dragon
decree-wind-dragon.description: +5 Mult if the play includes both a Wind and a Dragon

decree-all-suits.name: All Suits
decree-all-suits.description: +8 Mult if the play includes Characters, Circles and Bamboo

decree-bookends.name: Bookends
decree-bookends.description: +60 Points if the play includes both a 1 and a 9

decree-supernova.name: Supernova
decree-supernova.description: ×2.5 Mult if this play brings the round score to at least twice the target, before Supernova and Perfectionist bonuses.

decree-perfectionist.name: Perfectionist
decree-perfectionist.description: ×3 Mult if the first play clears the round, before Supernova and Perfectionist bonuses.

decree-wealth-engine.name: Wealth Engine
decree-wealth-engine.description: +1 Gold per Decree owned at the end of each round

decree-perpetual-motion.name: Perpetual Motion
decree-perpetual-motion.description: +2 Mult for each earlier play this run

decree-terminal-resonance.name: Terminal Resonance
decree-terminal-resonance.description: Every Terminal (1 or 9) played scores three times

decree-honor-resonance.name: Honor Resonance
decree-honor-resonance.description: Every Honor (Wind or Dragon) played scores three times

decree-manzu-monarch.name: Monarch of Characters
decree-manzu-monarch.description: ×2 Mult if every played tile is Characters

decree-pinzu-potentate.name: Potentate of Circles
decree-pinzu-potentate.description: ×2 Mult if every played tile is Circles

decree-souzu-sovereign.name: Sovereign of Bamboo
decree-souzu-sovereign.description: ×2 Mult if every played tile is Bamboo

decree-nature-bond.name: Nature Bond
decree-nature-bond.description: +3 Mult per Flower, +30 Points per Season

decree-honitsu-herald.name: Half Flush Herald
decree-honitsu-herald.description: ×2 Mult when you score a Half Flush: a complete hand of one suit plus Winds or Dragons

decree-sanshoku-sage.name: Triple Sequence Sage
decree-sanshoku-sage.description: ×2 Mult when you score a Mixed Triple Sequence: a complete hand with the same sequence in all three suits

decree-chanta-champion.name: Outside Hand Champion
decree-chanta-champion.description: ×2 Mult when you score an Outside Hand: a complete hand with at least one sequence, where every group and the pair includes a 1, 9, Wind or Dragon. A Pure Outside Hand (the same, but with no Winds or Dragons, so every group and the pair includes a 1 or 9) also counts.

decree-mandate-breaker.name: Mandate Breaker
decree-mandate-breaker.description: During Boss rounds: +15 Mult and ×1.5 Mult

decree-fortune-and-glory.name: Fortune and Glory
decree-fortune-and-glory.description: +60 Points and +8 Mult, and +3 Gold at the end of each round

decree-golden-age.name: Golden Age
decree-golden-age.description: +8 Gold at the end of each round

decree-blueprint.name: Blueprint
decree-blueprint.description: Copies the effect of the Decree to its right

decree-photograph.name: Photograph
decree-photograph.description: ×2 Mult if the play includes an Honor (a Wind or Dragon)

decree-transmuter.name: Transmuter
decree-transmuter.description: Played 2–8 tiles score as Terminals (1s and 9s)

decree-harmonizer.name: Harmonizer
decree-harmonizer.description: Sequences may mix suits (for example, 1 of Characters, 2 of Circles, 3 of Bamboo)

decree-heavens-wrath.name: Heaven's Wrath
decree-heavens-wrath.description: ×4 Mult if the play has no 2–8 tiles (only 1s, 9s, Winds and Dragons)

decree-void-blessing.name: Void Blessing
decree-void-blessing.description: ×5 Mult if every played tile is a Wind or Dragon

decree-eternal-echo.name: Eternal Echo
decree-eternal-echo.description: Every scoring tile scores three times

decree-dragon-king.name: Dragon King
decree-dragon-king.description: Every Dragon played scores four times

decree-yaku-amplifier.name: Yaku Amplifier
decree-yaku-amplifier.description: When a complete hand scores Yaku, its combined Yaku multiplier is multiplied by 1.5

decree-yakuman-seeker.name: Yakuman Seeker
decree-yakuman-seeker.description: ×5 Mult when you score a Yakuman, a top-tier hand such as Big Three Dragons or Thirteen Orphans

decree-eternal-garden.name: Eternal Garden
decree-eternal-garden.description: +10 Mult per Flower. Drought cannot suppress your Flowers.

decree-midas-touch.name: Midas Touch
decree-midas-touch.description: +10 Gold at the end of each round

decree-brainstorm.name: Brainstorm
decree-brainstorm.description: Copies the effect of your leftmost Decree

decree-doppelganger.name: Doppelganger
decree-doppelganger.description: Copies a random non-copy Decree on acquisition and at each round start.

decree-manzu-god.name: God of Characters
decree-manzu-god.description: ×3 Mult if every played tile is Characters

decree-pinzu-god.name: God of Circles
decree-pinzu-god.description: ×3 Mult if every played tile is Circles

decree-souzu-god.name: God of Bamboo
decree-souzu-god.description: ×3 Mult if every played tile is Bamboo

decree-glass-cannon.name: Glass Cannon
decree-glass-cannon.description: ×6 Mult. Destroyed if you lose a Boss round.

decree-phoenix.name: Phoenix
decree-phoenix.description: If you would lose a round, you clear it instead. This Decree is then destroyed.

decree-exponential.name: Exponential
decree-exponential.description: ×1.3 Mult per 100 base Points in the play

decree-chain-reaction.name: Chain Reaction
decree-chain-reaction.description: ×1.5 Mult per Yaku in the scored hand

decree-celestial-throne.name: Celestial Throne
decree-celestial-throne.description: ×10 Mult; −2 rack spaces and −1 Turn per round

decree-void-emperor.name: Void Emperor
decree-void-emperor.description: ×8 Mult if your previous play scored 0

decree-infinite-loop.name: Infinite Loop
decree-infinite-loop.description: Every scoring tile scores four times

decree-echo-dimension.name: Echo Dimension
decree-echo-dimension.description: Doubles the extra scorings your other Decrees grant (a tile that scores twice scores three times)

decree-clone-army.name: Clone Army
decree-clone-army.description: Copies the effects of all your other Decrees

decree-world-tree.name: World Tree
decree-world-tree.description: ×2 Mult per Flower and ×1.5 Mult per active Season

decree-philosophers-stone.name: Philosopher's Stone
decree-philosophers-stone.description: Doubles the Gold you earn from plays, REDRAW, items and round payouts (not from selling Decrees or from Omens)

decree-yaku-nexus.name: Yaku Nexus
decree-yaku-nexus.description: Every Yaku scores as if it were one tier higher (a Tier 1 ×1.3 becomes ×1.6)

decree-yakuman-blessing.name: Yakuman Blessing
decree-yakuman-blessing.description: ×10 Mult when you score a Yakuman, a top-tier hand such as Big Three Dragons or Thirteen Orphans

decree-reality-warp.name: Reality Warp
decree-reality-warp.description: Any 14 tiles you select can form a complete hand

decree-immortal-decree.name: Immortal Decree
decree-immortal-decree.description: Whenever you would lose a round, you clear it instead. After the first rescue, your scores are halved for the rest of the run, even if you sell this Decree.

river_tax.name: River Tax
river_tax.description: Gain 2 Gold each time you REDRAW.

tanyao_dispensation.name: Simples Dispensation
tanyao_dispensation.description: All Simples (normally only 2–8 tiles) also accepts 1s and 9s. Winds and Dragons still break it.

moonlit_seal.name: Moonlit Seal
moonlit_seal.description: Each Wind or Dragon played adds 0.1 to this Decree’s ×Mult (three give ×1.3).

pure_suit_asceticism.name: Pure Suit Asceticism
pure_suit_asceticism.description: ×1.1 Mult for each played tile of the play’s most common suit, compounding (five give about ×1.6).

broken_stair_edict.name: Broken Stair Edict
broken_stair_edict.description: Sequences may skip one number (1-3-4 or 1-2-4 counts).

false_eye_mandate.name: False Eye Mandate
false_eye_mandate.description: A complete hand may use one of its groups in place of the pair.

honor_transmutation.name: Honor Transmutation
honor_transmutation.description: Winds and Dragons may count as numbered tiles of your most common suit.

yakuman_succession.name: Yakuman Succession
yakuman_succession.description: While you hold at least 2 Flowers, these hands become Yakuman, the top tier (×4 each): Half Flush, Full Flush, Twice Pure Double Sequence (two pairs of identical sequences), Pure Outside Hand (a 1 or 9 in every group and the pair) and Seven Pairs. A hand weakened by a Mandate cannot rise. Copies do not stack.

celestial_wildcard.name: Celestial Wildcard
celestial_wildcard.description: One tile per play can stand in for any tile you need.

dead_wall_writ.name: Dead Wall Writ
dead_wall_writ.description: Once per round, swap one selected tile for a tile from the Dead Wall (the reserved tiles at the back of the wall) without spending a Turn.

shanten_clemency.name: Shanten Clemency
shanten_clemency.description: A hand one tile short of complete can be played as a complete hand, at half score.

closed_hand_austerity.name: Closed-Hand Austerity
closed_hand_austerity.description: Each complete Mahjong hand gains ×1.5, growing ×1.2 for every earlier complete hand this run, up to ×4 before Flower bonuses. Smaller plays and hands finished by Shanten Clemency do not count.

terminal_devotion.name: Terminal Devotion
terminal_devotion.description: Each Terminal (1 or 9) played adds 0.05 to this Decree’s ×Mult (four give ×1.2).

yaku_repetition_charter.name: Yaku Repetition Charter
yaku_repetition_charter.description: A Yaku scored in back-to-back rounds gains ×1.2 for each earlier round in its streak, up to ×4 before Flower bonuses. A round without it ends that streak.

codexFlora.empowerment: Each held Flower also empowers numerical Decree rewards by 10%. Set bonuses use distinct Flowers currently held, not every Flower ever collected.
codexFlora.awakeningLifecycle: Rebloom eligibility carries into future runs. The first copy is ordinary; once eligible, a duplicate awakens that Flower for this run. More duplicates do not stack powers or add slots. A new run resets awakenings, not eligibility.
codexFlora.chrysanthemumSet: With all four Flowers held, the awakened factor becomes ×{{factor}} per concealed meld instead. Pairs and loose tiles add no steps.
codexFlora.drought: Drought suspends Flower powers, including awakenings and Decree empowerment, unless an active Eternal Garden protects them. It does not delete Flowers, earned awakenings or collection slots.
codexFlora.distinction: Flowers awaken; Seasons do not. A Season is either normal or corrupted. Drawn bonus tiles are revealed and replaced automatically, without spending a Turn.
codexFlora.corruption: From Act 2, a Season may be corrupted instead of granting its normal effect. Ghost Parlor permits corruption from Act 1. Corrupted Seasons last only this round; they are not awakened Seasons.
codexFlora.interactionsIntro: These combinations need the Flower's powers and the normal Season to be active together. No awakening is required. Open a pairing for its optional recipe; merely previewing a play earns nothing.
codexFlora.orchidSpring: Drawing a Wind or Dragon while Orchid and Spring are active earns one extra Dead Wall draw. Extra draws do not chain, and an empty Dead Wall creates no tile. Extra tiles may temporarily exceed rack capacity.
codexFlora.bambooSummer: Play at least four physical terminal tiles (suited 1s or 9s) with Bamboo and Summer active. Summer-reserved tiles return to the live wall, and later Summers cannot shrink it again this round. The score bonus remains.
codexFlora.plumAutumn: Each scored physical sequence can return the most recent matching tile from the river, if the round continues. Only tiles already in the river before the play qualify. Each is recovered once, never copied; virtual or substituted faces do not qualify.
codexFlora.chrysanthemumWinter: With Chrysanthemum active, concealed plays ignore Winter's score penalty while keeping its one-rank-gap sequence rule. Open plays still pay the penalty. Drought blocks this protection unless the Flower is protected.
codexFlora.catalystsIntro: Selected direct Decree offers in the Tea House allow a Flower instead of Gold. Choose the exact owned Flower and confirm; this is optional and never an automatic sacrifice.
codexFlora.catalystsCost: Losing the Flower also reduces its set bonuses. The purchase is blocked if your remaining slots cannot hold the build. Recollecting it restores its earned awakening for this run. Yakuman Succession still needs two held Flowers, so paying with one requires at least three beforehand.

welcome.title: Welcome to Tensho!
welcome.p1: <0>Tensho (天翔)</0> means "Heavenly Ascent" in Japanese. It is a <3>roguelike game</3> of <6>poker-style hands</6> played with Mahjong tiles.
welcome.p2: Your goal is simple: <2>build scoring hands</2> and reach the target score each round. Fail to reach the target, and your run ends.
welcome.note1: Don't worry if you've never played Mahjong before! This tutorial will teach you everything you need to know, step by step.

hands.title: Hands You Can Play
hands.p1: A play can hold up to {{max}} tiles. It scores as the best hand its tiles make:
hands.mahjong: A complete Mahjong hand adds +{{mult}} Mult on top of its Yaku.

ready.title: You're Ready!
ready.note1: You can <1>reroll</1> the shop offerings for 5 gold. Each reroll costs +1 more.
ready.note2: Holding <1>25+ gold</1> maximizes interest! But spending on good decrees is usually worth more.
ready.p1: Don't worry about memorizing everything — you'll learn by playing!
ready.note3: Open the Codex from the main menu whenever you need a refresher.

game_concept.p1: Unlike traditional Mahjong which is played against opponents, Tensho is a <1>single-player puzzle game</1>. You're racing against the score target, not other players.
game_concept.p2: Each run consists of multiple <2>Acts</2>, and each Act has <5>3 Rounds</5>. The score targets increase as you progress.
game_concept.p3: Between rounds, you'll visit the <2>Tea House</2> (shop) to acquire powerful <5>Decrees</5> that modify the rules and boost your scoring potential.

tiles_overview.p1: The game uses <1>144 tiles</1> in total:

numbered_suits.note1: In the standard wall, each tile appears <1>4 times</1>. This is important for planning your hand!
numbered_suits.p1: There are <1>three numbered suits</1>, each with tiles ranked 1-9:
numbered_suits.p2: <0>Characters (萬子 / Manzu)</0> — Feature Chinese numerals with the character 萬 (wan, meaning "ten thousand")
numbered_suits.p3: <0>Circles (筒子 / Pinzu)</0> — Show circular patterns representing coins or dots
numbered_suits.p4: <0>Bamboo (索子 / Souzu)</0> — Depict bamboo sticks (the 1 of Bamboo shows a bird instead)

terminals_simples.p1: Numbered tiles are divided into two important categories:

wind_tiles.note1: Terminals are worth double the points of simples! Many yaku also specifically require or exclude terminals.
wind_tiles.p1: There are <1>four Wind tiles</1>, representing the cardinal directions:
wind_tiles.p2: Wind tiles are <1>Honor tiles</1> and are worth <4>50 points</4> each, 100 inside a group — the highest base value!

dragon_tiles.note1: Winds cannot form sequences. They can only form triplets or pairs.
dragon_tiles.p2: <0>白 (White Dragon / Haku)</0> — A blank or framed tile, representing purity or emptiness
dragon_tiles.p3: <0>發 (Green Dragon / Hatsu)</0> — The character 發 in green, meaning "prosperity" or "to emit"
dragon_tiles.p4: <0>中 (Red Dragon / Chun)</0> — The character 中 in red, meaning "center" or "middle"
dragon_tiles.p5: Dragons are <1>Honor tiles</1> worth <4>15 points</4>, and every Dragon that scores adds +2 Mult, +4 inside a group. They cannot form sequences.

bonus_tiles.p1: <0>Bonus tiles</0> are special tiles that don't form part of your hand:

sequences.note1: When you draw a bonus tile, it's immediately revealed and you draw a replacement tile. Flowers and Seasons provide scaling bonuses and effects!
sequences.p1: A <1>sequence</1> is <4>3 consecutive tiles of the same suit</4>.

melds_overview.p1: A <1>meld</1> (also called a "group" or "set") is a specific combination of tiles:
melds_overview.p2: Understanding melds is <1>essential</1> — your winning hand is made up of these building blocks!

quads.li1: Sequences must be in the <1>same suit</1>
quads.p1: A <1>quad</1> (also called "kong" or "kan") is <4>4 identical tiles</4>.
quads.p2: Quads are the rarest meld type: in the standard wall they use all 4 copies of a tile!

pairs.p2: Every standard winning hand requires <2>exactly one pair</2>. This is sometimes called the "head" (雀頭) of the hand.

winning_hand.note1: Triplets are worth <1>+40 points</1> — more than sequences (+30)! However, they're harder to complete since you need 3 of the same tile, and the standard wall holds only 4 copies of each.
winning_hand.li1: Worth <1>+65 points</1> — the most of any meld
winning_hand.li2: Counts as a single meld despite having 4 tiles
winning_hand.li3: When declared, you draw a replacement tile
winning_hand.p1: A standard winning hand consists of:

gameplay_overview.note1: The pair is worth <1>+15 points</1>. Any tile can form a pair — numbered tiles, winds, or dragons.

drawing.p2: The <1>wall</1> starts with 70 drawable tiles (after the dead wall is reserved). Watch the remaining tiles counter!

base_points.note1: When you draw a <1>bonus tile</1> (Flower or Season), it's automatically revealed and you draw a replacement. This doesn't cost a turn!

yaku_intro.p2: There are <1>20 yaku</1> in Tensho, organized into 4 tiers:

decree_categories.note1: Yaku <1>stack multiplicatively</1>! A hand with ×1.3 and ×2.0 yaku gets ×2.6 total. Build combos for massive scores!

acts_rounds.p1: Your run is divided into <1>Acts</1>, and each Act contains <3>3 Rounds</3>:
acts_rounds.p2: Score targets increase with each Act. Act 1 starts easy, but by Act 6 you'll need powerful combos to survive!

decree_slots.note1: Some Decrees can help counter specific mandates. Plan your build accordingly!
decree_slots.li1: <0>Modify scoring</0> — Add multipliers or flat bonuses
decree_slots.li2: <0>Bend rules</0> — Change what makes a legal hand

decree_slots.p1: You have a limited number of <1>Decree Slots</1>. You start with <3>5 slots</3> and can earn more through:

decrees_intro.p1: <0>Decrees (法令)</0> are rule-modifying cards that persist throughout your run. Think of them as Tensho's equivalent of "Jokers" in Balatro.

flowers_system.p1: <0>Flowers</0> provide <3>permanent bonuses</3> that last your entire run:
flowers_system.p2: Collecting multiple flowers unlocks <2>set bonuses</2>: 2 flowers = +1 decree slot, 4 flowers = double flower effectiveness!

interest.note1: Higher rarity decrees are more expensive and rarer in the shop. Build synergies between multiple common decrees for powerful combos!

turns.title: How a Round Works
turns.p1: Each round gives you {{turns}} Turns. Every Turn is one of two actions:
turns.play: score the selected tiles: up to {{max}}, or a whole Mahjong hand.
turns.redraw: send any number of selected tiles to the river and draw new ones.
turns.p2: Reach the round's target before your Turns run out. Your last Turn is always a play, and items can give free redraws that cost no Turn.
turns.warning: Run out of Turns below the target and the run is over.

select.title: Selecting Tiles
select.p1: Tap rack tiles to select them. The Hand score in the middle of the table shows what your selection would score right now: the hand it makes, its Points and its Mult.
select.p2: Selecting is free: nothing is spent until you press Play hand or REDRAW. A play scores as the best hand its tiles make, so try a few selections before you commit.
select.note: The biggest score isn't always the best play. Check which useful tiles would stay on your rack for the next Turn.

refill.title: Drawing Tiles
refill.p1: After a play or REDRAW, replacement tiles are drawn from the wall. Normally this refills your rack, but a nearly empty wall or an active effect can change the draw.

redraw.title: REDRAW
redraw.p1: Select the tiles you don't want, as many as you like, and press REDRAW. They go to the river and new tiles take their place.
redraw.li1: Free redraws from items are used first; otherwise a REDRAW costs one Turn.
redraw.li2: Redrawn tiles stay in the river for the rest of the round.
redraw.li3: Some Decrees reward each REDRAW, a Boss Mandate can forbid it, and Seasons can change its cost. Check the active effects first.
redraw.note: Keep the tiles that already make a group, and redraw the loners.

score.title: How Scoring Works
score.note: Bigger hands, Dragons, Orbs and Decrees all raise the Mult, and the Mult multiplies everything.

points.title: Tile Points
points.p1: Every tile in a group scores its points:
points.note: Winds are worth ten times a simple tile; Dragons add Mult instead. A pair or bigger group doubles either. A numbered tile outside any group scores half.

groups.title: Group Bonuses
groups.p1: Each group adds bonus points on top of its tiles:
groups.example: Example: Two Pairs = {{pair}} + {{pair}} = +{{total}} bonus points, and the second group adds +1 Mult.

swift.title: Swift Clears
swift.p1: Rounds can't be skipped. Clear a Small or Large round with {{spare}} or more Turns to spare to earn an Omen.
swift.li1: You still collect the round's Gold and visit the Tea House.
swift.li2: Boss rounds never give an Omen.
swift.note: A strong early hand saves Turns, and saved Turns become Omens.

saving.title: Saving Your Run
saving.p1: Your run is saved in this browser after every completed action. Choose {{saveLeave}} to return to the menu, then {{resume}} to continue at the table or in the Tea House.
saving.li1: Wait for {{saved}} before closing the tab. If saving fails, keep the tab open and press {{retry}}.
saving.li2: Saves stay in this browser on this device. Clearing site data or switching browsers leaves them behind.
saving.li3: Selected tiles and animations are not restored. Updates wait until you leave the table safely; your saved run is kept.

guide.title: How to play
guide.intro: Tensho is a poker-style game played with Mahjong tiles. Pick tiles that form a hand, play it for points, and reach each round’s target.
guide.redrawHelp: sends any number of selected tiles to the river and draws new ones.
guide.turnsHelp: Each round gives you {{turns}} Turns. Play hand and REDRAW each cost one; free redraws cost none, and your last Turn must be a play. Clear a Small or Large round with {{spare}} Turns to spare to earn an Omen.
guide.scoreHelp: Points are the tiles’ values plus each group’s bonus. Mult starts at 1 and grows with bigger hands, Dragons, Orbs and Decrees. Numbered tiles outside a group score half.
guide.patternRule: Every group after the first adds +1 Mult. Triplets and Straights of Four add +1 more, Quads and Straights of Five +2. Normally each tile counts once, and a play holds up to 6 tiles unless it is a full Mahjong hand.
guide.tilesHelp: Characters show Chinese numbers 一 to 九; Circles and Bamboo show their count (the 1 of Bamboo is a bird). You can turn numbers on the tiles on in Settings.
guide.honorsHelp: Winds are worth {{wind}} points each, {{windGroup}} in a group. Each Dragon adds +{{dragon}} Mult, +{{dragonGroup}} in a group.
guide.specialHelp: A coloured frame with a gem is a mark, a wax stamp is a seal, and a shimmer is an edition. A tile holds only one of them.

Pairs.name: Pairs
Pairs.covers: Pair, Two Pairs or Three Pairs (a pair is two identical tiles). The Seven Pairs hand has its own family.

Pinfu.name: Sequences
Pinfu.covers: Sequence, Sequence + Pair or Two Sequences (a sequence is three consecutive numbers of one suit), and All Sequences: a complete hand of four sequences plus a pair that is not Dragons or East Wind.

Ittsu.name: Straights
Ittsu.covers: Straight of Four, Straight of Five or Straight + Pair (consecutive numbers of one suit), and a 1–9 Straight: a complete hand holding 1-2-3, 4-5-6 and 7-8-9 of one suit.

Toitoi.name: Sets
Toitoi.covers: Triplet, Full House, Two Triplets, Triplet + Sequence, Quad or Quad + Pair (a triplet is three identical tiles, a quad four), and All Triplets: a complete hand of four triplets or quads plus a pair.

Yakuhai.name: Honors
Yakuhai.covers: Any play with a group made only of Winds or Dragons, and Value Tiles: a complete hand with a triplet or quad of Dragons or East Wind.

Tanyao.name: All Simples
Tanyao.covers: Any play that forms a group and uses only 2–8 tiles, with no 1s, 9s, Winds or Dragons (Stones are ignored), and All Simples: a complete hand of only 2–8 tiles.

Honitsu.name: Half Flush
Honitsu.covers: Half Flush: a complete hand of one suit plus Winds or Dragons. A shorter play of one suit does not count.

Chinitsu.name: Full Flush
Chinitsu.covers: Full Flush: a complete hand of one suit only, with no Winds or Dragons. A shorter play of one suit does not count.

Sanshoku.name: Mixed Triple
Sanshoku.covers: Mixed Triple Sequence: a complete hand with the same sequence in all three suits, such as 2-3-4 in Characters, Circles and Bamboo.

SevenPairs.name: Seven Pairs
SevenPairs.covers: Seven Pairs: a complete hand of exactly seven different pairs (14 tiles). Shorter plays of pairs belong to the Pairs family.

Chanta.name: Outside Hand
Chanta.covers: Outside Hand: a complete hand with at least one sequence, where every group and the pair includes a 1, 9, Wind or Dragon. A Pure Outside Hand (the same, but with no Winds or Dragons) also counts.

Kokushi.name: Thirteen Orphans
Kokushi.covers: Thirteen Orphans: a complete hand with one of every 1, 9, Wind and Dragon, plus one duplicate of any of them.

All.name: Every family
All.covers: All 12 hand families, Pairs and Seven Pairs included.
